title: Variables should not be self-assigned
description: Self-assignment occurs when a variable is assigned to itself, such as `x = x` or `self.attribute = self.attribute`. This is almost always a mistake and indicates dead code, a copy-paste error, or incomplete refactoring. Self-assignments have no effect on program execution and should be removed or corrected to assign the intended value.
message: Remove or correct this self-assignment of variable '{{variable_name}}'.

impact.reliability: Medium impact as self-assignments indicate logical errors and dead code that should be removed
impact.maintainability: High impact on code clarity as self-assignments confuse readers and indicate incomplete implementation

recommendation: Remove the self-assignment statement entirely if it serves no purpose, or correct it to assign the intended value from a different source.

references.title: SonarSource Python Rules - Variables should not be self-assigned

noncompliant.code:
x = 5
x = x  # Self-assignment has no effect
print(x)

numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
numbers[2] = numbers[2]  # No effect
print(numbers)

compliant.description: Proper variable assignment with different source
compliant.code:
x = 5
y = x  # Assigning to different variable
print(y)

numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
numbers[2] = 99  # Assigning new value
print(numbers)

config = {'timeout': 30, 'retries': 3}
config['timeout'] = 60  # Updating with new value

devsecops.automation: High - Can be automatically detected through AST analysis
devsecops.compliance: Medium - Improves code quality and prevents logical errors

why_is_this_an_issue: Self-assignments are statements where a variable is assigned to itself, which has no computational effect. These typically occur due to copy-paste errors, incomplete refactoring, or misunderstanding of the assignment operation. Such statements waste processing time (though minimally) and more importantly indicate incomplete or incorrect code logic. They make the codebase confusing for maintainers who may spend time trying to understand the purpose of a seemingly meaningless operation.

how_to_fix.description: Identify the self-assignment statement in your code
Determine if the statement serves any purpose - most self-assignments are mistakes
If it's a mistake, remove the self-assignment statement entirely
If it was meant to assign a different value, correct the right-hand side to use the intended source
Review surrounding code to ensure the fix doesn't break intended logic
Test the code to verify the change works as expected

conditions.comment: Check if target and value have same identifier - simple variable case
